info.title: Divide the list
info.text:
Merge sort splits a list into smaller parts.

Continue until single-item lists remain.

A single-item list is already sorted.

Challenge: Why can splitting stop at one item?

A single item cannot be out of order relative to another item in its list.

info.title: Merge sorted groups
info.text:
Compare the front unmerged values.

Take the smaller value into the output.

Append the remainder when one group empties.

Challenge: Which value is chosen after 2? Why?

3, because it is smaller than the other front value, 7.

info.title: Read a merge segment
info.text:
Read from each sorted input group.

Advance only the pointer you used.

Do not discard unmerged values.

Challenge: Why increment only the pointer used?

The other front value has not been output yet and must remain available for comparison.

info.title: Insert into a prefix
info.text:
Treat the first item as a sorted prefix.

Take the next item as the key.

Insert the key at its correct position.

Challenge: What is the sorted prefix after inserting 5?

2, 5, 6. The final value 1 has not yet been inserted.

info.title: Shift and insert
info.text:
Save the key before shifting.

Move larger prefix values one position right.

Place the key in the gap.

Challenge: Why save the key before shifting values?

Shifting could overwrite its original position. Saving it preserves the value for insertion.

info.title: Compare the methods
info.text:
Bubble sort compares neighbours over passes.

Insertion sort grows a sorted prefix.

Merge sort splits and merges sorted groups.

Challenge: Which method can use few shifts on nearly sorted data?

Insertion sort, because many keys are already close to their correct positions.
